foot_tag: author's works · our review · the author has the final word
section_lead: Works by independent researchers — with our review and the author's response.
section_what: The author sends their work by email. We read it in full, retell it in our own words, write a review, and show it all to the author. We publish only with their consent, along with their comment.
honest_note: These are not peer-reviewed publications. There is no journal review or anyone's approval behind them — just our analysis and the work of the person who made it. We check whether it is done seriously: there is a problem statement, method, data, or conclusion. Then judge for yourself: the author's original version is attached to each work.
how1_s: By email, with their text, data, and links. Free, and we always reply.
how2_s: We read it in full and write a review: what is strong, what could be improved, and what remains unclear. We help, not nitpick.
how3_s: They see the review before publication, add their comment, and decide whether the work goes live.
empty_note: Nothing here yet. Works appear as they are submitted and as we manage to review them.
invite_p: We review works by those who research outside institutions: students, engineers, independent researchers. One condition — the work is done seriously and relates to natural sciences or engineering. The review is free. Your name will appear on the page only if you provide it; otherwise, a public work code will be used instead. The final word in publication is yours, and you can remove it at any time without explanation. We will send formatting guidelines and a preparation prompt in reply to your email: work prepared accordingly is reviewed faster and more accurately.
privacy_note: We never publish the author's contact details — neither email nor profile links. You can send a message to the author through us.
badge_title: The work was submitted by the author, and the review below is ours. This is not a preprint archive publication.
badge_note: The work was sent to us by the author; the review below is ours. It has no journal review; the author's original version is attached in full.
kind_title: Type of work: it determines what we ask the author and what we advise.
author_hint: The author did not identify themselves. Instead of a name, there is a public work code: you can use it to find and cite the work.
review_intro: We look at the methodology and say what could be improved. This is an outside perspective, not an evaluation or a verdict.
author_word_h2: The author has the final word
author_word_note: We show the review to the author before publication. Their response follows and remains without our objection.
rights_note: The author can remove the work from publication at any time and without explanation — just send an email.
source_note: Everything the author sent: text, data, appendices, and links — without our edits or cuts.
similar_note: Selected by common topics — from our reviews and from this section.
our_note: Our retelling in our own words, at three levels of depth — from one paragraph to a detailed analysis. The author's exact text remains in the original.
prep_lead: We retell research in plain language — free, in five languages, with your original beside it and your name on it. This page is everything you need to know before you send us a paper. It takes about ten minutes.
prep_why_h2: Why we ask for anything at all
prep_why_p: We are a small team and we read every paper ourselves. The two things below — a self-check and a short cover note — are not gatekeeping: they let us answer you in days instead of weeks, and they make the retelling better, because they tell us what you consider the heart of the work. Nothing here is graded. Nobody is rejected for a weak self-check.
prep_s1_s: Copy the prompt below into any language model you like — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, whichever you already use — together with your paper. Keep the answer.
prep_s2_t: Write two or three sentences of your own
prep_s2_s: What you would want a reader to remember a week later. This matters more than the self-check: it is the only part nobody can write for you.
prep_s3_t: Send it all in one letter
prep_s3_s: The paper (PDF), the self-check answer, your sentences, and the licence you want. Write to article@bridge42worlds.academy — one letter, no forms, no account.
prep_prompt_note: Copy it as it is. It is written to be blunt with you, not kind — that is what makes it useful.
prep_prompt_text:
You are reviewing a scientific manuscript before its author submits it to
bridge42worlds, a site that retells research in plain language, free of charge, in five
languages.

Read the attached paper and answer in English, briefly and without flattery:

1. In two sentences: what did the authors actually do, and what came out of it?
2. What is genuinely new here, compared with what was already known?
3. Which claim is the weakest — where would a careful reader push back first?
4. What is missing that a reader outside this field would need: a definition, a scale,
   a comparison, a control?
5. Who benefits if this result holds — and roughly when?
6. Is anything in the text that cannot be supported by the data shown?

Then write, in 120 words or less, a plain-language summary a curious non-specialist could
follow: no jargon, no formulas, one clear image.

Be direct. If the work is thin, say so — the author asked you, not a reviewer.
prep_order_note: Every step is a letter from a person, not a status page.
prep_o1_s: Within a day, usually the same one.
prep_o2_s: If the work is outside what we can honestly retell, we say so plainly and explain why. That is the only kind of refusal we send.
prep_o3_s: Plain language, in five languages, with figures from your paper and a cover image. Usually a few days.
prep_o4_t: You read it before anyone else
prep_o4_s: Nothing is published until you have seen it. Corrections are expected, not an inconvenience — this is your work.
prep_o5_t: It goes live at a permanent address
prep_o5_s: With your name, the original file, and the licence you chose. It appears in search, in our feed, and on your author page.
prep_r1: The work stays yours. We do not take any rights to it.
prep_r2: Nothing is published until you have read it and said yes.
prep_r3: You can have it taken down at any time, without explaining why — one letter is enough.
prep_r4: We never publish your email, your affiliation, or anything you did not put in the paper.
prep_r5: Free. Now and later. We do not charge authors and we do not sell placement.
prep_license_p: Tell us which licence your work is under, or which one you want. We recommend CC BY 4.0 — it lets anyone reuse the work as long as they credit you, which is what most researchers want anyway. If you prefer something more restrictive, that is fine: we publish the retelling and link to the original, and we mark the licence on every page.
